sections.html:
Covington sits where the Licking River meets the Ohio, facing downtown Cincinnati across the water. It is Northern Kentucky's biggest city and shares the Kenton County seat with Independence. About 41,847 people lived here by the July 2025 estimate, a 2.2 percent rise over 2020, packed into 13.20 square miles of land. That density explains the street grid of rowhouses, cottages and mansions.

The city has 19 neighborhoods, many inside 12 historic districts in its northern half, and many houses date from the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. Sellers of those homes should be ready for buyers' questions on wiring, plumbing, foundations and whether the lot lies inside a historic district. Annexations in recent decades pushed the boundary south, which is where newer subdivisions sit.

Values run below much of the Cincinnati area. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $187,300, median gross rent is $1,006, and owner costs with a mortgage run $1,404 a month. Median household income is $61,166 across 18,265 households. About half of homes, 51.8%, are lived in by their owners, which makes rentals common.

I-71, I-75 and US 25 reach downtown, and the Transit Authority of Northern Kentucky runs the buses. Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky International Airport, Kentucky's largest, is one of DHL's three superhubs. Offices, health care and the airport drive jobs, with Fidelity Investments, Club Chef and St. Elizabeth Hospital among the larger employers. A four-story OneNKY Center opened in September 2025 with a biotech lab and startup incubator.

sections.h2: Which school district covers an address?
sections.html: Covington Independent Public Schools covers most of the city and is the largest independent district in Kentucky. The southern edge of Covington falls instead in the Kenton County School District. Catholic families have Covington Latin School and Holy Cross High School, and Calvary Christian School is a Baptist option. Tell buyers which district the address belongs to, since the choice follows the house.

A landlord needs an occupational license plus a separate rental license. Unlicensed operators have been cited at $250, $500 and $750 for first, second and third offenses, with a vacate order possible if citations are ignored. Rental licenses cost $30 for a one-unit parcel up to $150 for 100-plus units, last three years and require an inspection.

  • Rentals of 29 days or less need a short-term license each year.
  • The June 2024 ordinance set the annual short-term fee at $500, renewal at $250, a failed-inspection revisit at $100 and a change-of-use application at $80.
  • Non-host-occupied short-term licenses are limited to 151 citywide.
  • Code Enforcement handles maintenance, nuisance and zoning complaints and does periodic inspections. Call (859) 292-2167 with questions.

If you own a rental you plan to sell, check the license status first.

The Kenton County Sheriff bills and collects until the close of business on April 15. After that, the County Clerk takes the unpaid bill and holds a sale in July where a third party can buy it.

Kenton County sheriff: what a bill costs by payment date
Payment windowEffect on the bill
October 1 to November 12 percent reduction

February 1 to April 15Further penalties added, so call the sheriff for the figure
  • Pay in person at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 1200, Covington, or at the Independence courthouse, 5272 Madison Pike.
  • Mail checks to Kenton County Sheriff, P.O. Box 188070, Erlanger, KY 41018.
  • If no bill has come by October 15, call 859-392-1800.
  • Returned checks cost $50.

At closing the seller hands their share of the year to the buyer or the buyer's escrow company, after which the owner of record owes the entire bill. Write that into your contract.

Go through the Kenton County PVA, at 859-392-1750 or 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 3300. File a Review Request with burden-of-proof documents such as comparable sales, an appraisal, repair estimates or photos. The conference is informal, can run by email or by appointment, and may begin any time after January 1, but it must finish before the open inspection period ends each May. Clerk filings follow within days after that. A dissatisfied owner can then go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals.

The PVA's website also carries the homestead and disability exemption forms, plus sales dashboards and comparable-sales maps for houses and condominiums that help you build a case. Ask the office where your parcel stands in the reassessment cycle.

sections.h2: Selling an older or historic house
sections.html:
Many Covington houses are over a hundred years old, and buyers know it. Expect them to ask about the age of the roof, wiring, plumbing and foundation, and about any past water problems. If the lot sits inside a historic district, call the city before you plan exterior work to prepare for a sale, since changes to a street-facing facade may need approval first.

Gather what you have: receipts for major work, permits, inspection reports and any notes about repairs. A buyer who sees records is less likely to ask for a big credit. If you would rather not make repairs at all, an as-is sale to a cash buyer lets the next owner decide what to fix.

A title company or attorney runs the closing. You sign the deed, your mortgage and any open tax are paid from the proceeds, and the deed is recorded. Bring a photo ID and your keys, and ask for the settlement statement beforehand so you can check each line.

If you are selling a rental, hand over the leases and deposit records, and tell the buyer's side what happens to the tenant. If the house came through an estate, have the papers showing who may sign ready before the closing date. Sellers who move away should leave the sheriff a forwarding address, because the next bill goes to the owner of record and a missed notice means penalties for somebody.

A cash sale removes the steps that slow most listings. There is no lender appraisal that can come in low, no mortgage approval that can fall through, and no repair list after the inspection. You skip staging and showings too. County paperwork still applies, so the deed is recorded and any unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds, but you decide the closing date with the buyer instead of waiting on a bank.

1. Confirm whether the house is a rental, and check that every license is current.
  2. Ask the sheriff whether the current bill is paid, and the clerk about earlier years.
  3. Find out which school district serves the address.
  4. Get a mortgage payoff letter near the planned closing date.
  5. Decide in the contract who covers repairs on an older house.

A cash buyer takes an older Covington house as it stands, wiring and foundation questions included, and any unpaid tax or license problem is settled from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: What is Covington's latest population figure?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 41,847 people, a 2.2 percent rise over the 2020 base.

faqs.q: What does a typical Covington house cost?
faqs.a: The median owner-occupied value is $187,300, and 51.8 percent of homes are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Does a Covington landlord need a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. The city asks for an occupational license and a separate rental license, and unlicensed operators have been cited starting at $250.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax on a Covington house?
faqs.a: The Kenton County Sheriff, until April 15. Unpaid bills then move to the Kenton County Clerk.
Covington Independent Public Schools covers most of the city, while the Kenton County School District covers the southern portions.
